memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the fourteenth day of the first month the LORD's Passover is to be held. On the fifteenth day of this month there is to be a festival; for seven days eat bread made without yeast. On the first day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. - Num 28:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The calendar of worship now turns to the great festivals, beginning with Passover. This was the yearly remembrance of the night God delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt, when the blood of the lamb caused death to pass over their homes. For seven days they ate bread without yeast, recalling their hurried departure and their rescue by God's mighty hand.

Passover was Israel's celebration of redemption. Year after year, they remembered that they had once been slaves and that God had set them free. It kept the story of God's saving power alive in every generation. Their identity was rooted in this rescue: they were a redeemed people, belonging to the God who delivered them.

For us, Passover holds even deeper meaning, for it points directly to Christ. The apostle Paul declares plainly that Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed for us (1 Cor 5:7). The lamb whose blood spared Israel foreshadowed the Lamb whose blood saves us from sin and death. Every Passover pointed forward to Him.

The removal of yeast, which Scripture connects to sin, reminds us that those redeemed by Christ are called to live in purity and truth (1 Cor 5:8). We are a redeemed people, freed not from Egypt but from the slavery of sin. Remember your redemption, celebrate the Lamb who was slain, and live as one set free by the blood of Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you remember and celebrate your redemption in Christ?
2. How does Passover point you to Jesus, the true Passover Lamb?
3. What does it mean to live as a redeemed people, freed from sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are my Passover Lamb, sacrificed to set me free from sin and death. Help me to remember my redemption with joy and to live in the purity of those You have redeemed. Amen.
